core_obligations: Produce the finite pointwise data: for every point x of X_s choose a pointed elementary etale neighbourhood diagram with g^*F/X'/S' completely devissaged at x', and use openness of each g together with quasi-compactness of the fibre X_s to extract a finite subfamily with X_s = g_1(X'_{s'_1}) union ... union g_n(X'_{s'_n}) (proof lines 1589-1610).

Glue the finitely many base changes over one base: set S' = S'_1 x_S ... x_S S'_n and Y_i = X'_i x_{S'_i} S', so that a single elementary etale neighbourhood (S', s') -> (S, s) carries all n devissages simultaneously (proof lines 1611-1613).

Apply the base change lemma for complete devissages to each Y_i and conclude that the pullback of F to Y_i has a complete devissage over s, giving X_s = (X_{S'})_{s'} contained in the union of the h_i(Y_i) (proof lines 1613-1616).
proof_roadmap: Pointwise step: for x in X_s, the existence lemma for a complete devissage supplies a pointed elementary etale neighbourhood diagram whose pullback g^*F has a complete devissage at x' (proof lines 1589-1597).

Finiteness step: X_s is quasi-compact because X -> S is of finite type, and each g is open, so finitely many of the open sets g(X'_{s'}) cover X_s; label them g_i : X'_i -> X with bases (S'_i, s'_i) (proof lines 1598-1610).

Base change step: take the fibre product S' = S'_1 x_S ... x_S S'_n, a single elementary etale neighbourhood of s, and set Y_i = X'_i x_{S'_i} S'; the base change lemma transports each complete devissage to Y_i over s (proof lines 1611-1616).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts the existence of a whole family of etale morphisms h_i : Y_i -> X_{S'} over one elementary etale neighbourhood (S', s') -> (S, s), each Y_i carrying a complete devissage of the pullback of F and collectively covering the fibre X_s (statement lines 1580-1585). The non-routine step is the passage from the pointwise existence of a devissage at every x in X_s, which the author has available at each single point, to a single base change that works for all of them at once: the fibre must first be made finite using openness of the elementary etale morphisms and quasi-compactness of X_s, and the finitely many bases S'_i then have to be multiplied together over S before the base change lemma can be applied to every i simultaneously (proof lines 1598-1616). The author's own lead-in at source line 1573 calls this step bookkeeping, so the difficulty is the fibre-product bookkeeping rather than a new construction, which places it at H2.
